title: Chapter 8.3 — Graphing f(x) = ax² + bx + c

confusionCorner.title: Sign Errors in the Formula
confusionCorner.body: The formula is $ x = -\frac{b}{2a} $. If $ b $ is negative, $-b$ becomes positive. For $ f(x)=3x^2-2x $, $ b=-2 $, so $ -b = 2 $. [[imp:Don't forget the negative sign in front of the fraction!]]

explanation: For a quadratic function in standard form $ f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c $, the [[kw:axis of symmetry]] is the vertical line $$ x = -\frac{b}{2a} $$
The x-coordinate of the [[kw:vertex]] is also $ -\frac{b}{2a} $. To find the y-coordinate, substitute this x-value into the function: $ f\left(-\frac{b}{2a}\right) $.
If $ a > 0 $, the parabola opens [[imp:upward]], and the vertex is the minimum. If $ a < 0 $, it opens [[imp:downward]], and the vertex is the maximum.
The y-intercept is $ c $, because $ f(0) = c $.

blocks.title: Graphing f(x) = ax² + bx + c

explanation: To graph $ f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c $:
1. Find and graph the [[kw:axis of symmetry]] $ x = -\frac{b}{2a} $.
2. Find and plot the [[kw:vertex]] by plugging that x into $ f(x) $.
3. Use the [[kw:y-intercept]] $ (0, c) $, and reflect it across the axis of symmetry to get a matching point.
4. Draw a smooth parabola through these points. If needed, plot additional points.
The [[kw:domain]] is all real numbers. The [[kw:range]] is $ y \ge y_{\text{vertex}} $ if $ a>0 $, or $ y \le y_{\text{vertex}} $ if $ a<0 $.

formulaCard.formula: $$ \text{1. Axis: } x = -\frac{b}{2a} \quad \text{2. Vertex: } \left(-\frac{b}{2a}, f\left(-\frac{b}{2a}\right)\right) \quad \text{3. y-int: } (0, c) $$
notes: Reflect y-intercept across axis to get a symmetric point.
The parabola is symmetric; points equidistant from axis have same y.

formulaCard.title: Finding Maximum or Minimum Value

explanation: The y-coordinate of the vertex is the [[kw:maximum value]] if $ a < 0 $, or the [[kw:minimum value]] if $ a > 0 $.
To find the max/min: 1) Compute $ x = -\frac{b}{2a} $. 2) Substitute this x into the function to get $ f(x) $. That's the extreme value.
In word problems, the independent variable (often $ x $ or $ t $) tells you when the max/min occurs; the function value tells you what that max/min is.

blocks.title: Maximum and Minimum Values
teacherCues: Write f(x) = -4x² - 24x - 19. 'a is negative, so the parabola opens down. That means the vertex is a maximum.'
Then find the y-coordinate of the vertex: x = -b/(2a) = -(-24)/(2(-4)) = -3. f(-3) = 17. So the maximum value is 17.

confusionCorner.body: The question 'What is the maximum?' asks for the y-value. 'When does it reach the maximum?' asks for the x-value. In $ f(t) = -16t^2 + 80t + 5 $, max height is 105 ft, occurring at $ t = 2.5 $ seconds.

blocks.title: Real-Life: Lowest Point of a Suspension Cable

explanation: Many real-world structures (bridges, arches, cables) follow a parabolic shape modeled by $ y = ax^2 + bx + c $.
The [[kw:lowest point]] (if $ a > 0 $) or highest point (if $ a < 0 $) is the vertex of the parabola.
To find it: 1) Compute $ x = -\frac{b}{2a} $. 2) Substitute x to get y.
Example: $ y = 0.000098x^2 - 0.37x + 552 $. $ a=0.000098 > 0 $ → parabola opens up, vertex is minimum.
Vertex x ≈ 1888 ft, y ≈ 203 ft. The cable is about 203 ft above water at its lowest.

notes: For $ a > 0 $, the vertex is the minimum (lowest point).
For $ a < 0 $, the vertex is the maximum (highest point).

confusionCorner.title: Units Matter!
confusionCorner.body: In these models, x and y are in feet. The vertex x tells you how far from a reference point the lowest point occurs; the vertex y gives the height. Always check the units given in the problem.

discoveryHook.scenario: The cables of the Mackinac Bridge form a giant parabola. The lowest point is right at the vertex! By using $ x = -b/(2a) $, engineers can find exactly where the cable hangs closest to the water.

formulaCard.title: Complete Blueprint Formulas
notes: Symmetric point: from y-intercept, go equal distance opposite side of axis.

explanation: Understand: Identify $ a, b, c $. $ a $ tells direction (up/down) and whether vertex is max or min. $ c $ is y-intercept.
Solve – Graphing: 1) Axis: $ x = -\frac{b}{2a} $. 2) Vertex: $ (x_{\text{axis}}, f(x_{\text{axis}})) $. 3) y-intercept: $ (0, c) $; reflect across axis. 4) Plot and draw smooth curve.
Solve – Application: The vertex coordinates answer 'when' (x) and 'what' (y) for the extreme value.
Conclude: State domain (all reals) and range. For real-world problems, interpret vertex in context (time of max height, lowest cable point, etc.).
